rationale: C11 is a highly plausible direct template: it is the prior year's letter to the same recipient for the same Good Friday observance. Both letters move from the religious meaning of Good Friday to its effect on Christian citizens, spiritual renewal, human welfare, and the pursuit of peace. The later letter substantially recasts this distinctive message rather than merely sharing generic letter conventions. C08 and C12 have weaker parallels involving religious reflection, common humanity, prayer, and peace, but neither provides comparable occasion-specific drafting machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Throughout Christendom, Good Friday is observed as a day of solemn remembrance with the Churches of our land united in the recognition of its import.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: To the individual Christian, Good Friday is an occasion for intensifying his faith... this year's observance of Good Friday in the churches of Washington and of communities throughout the land
shared_material.explanation: Both open by defining the religious significance of Good Friday and situating its observance among Christians and churches throughout the land.

shared_material.child_excerpt: When our Christian citizens think on these things, they will be... strengthened by a new appreciation of the spiritual resources available to us all.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: this year's observance of Good Friday... will surely strengthen Americans in their endeavors to live as Christian citizens
shared_material.explanation: The later letter reuses the distinctive linkage between Good Friday observance, strengthening Americans, and Christian citizenship.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The price of peace, our ultimate objective, is unceasing sacrifice and prayer.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: those spiritual values which guide them in their quest for a just peace and for a better life for human beings everywhere on earth.
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude the reflection by connecting spiritual resources or values to peace and improved human welfare.
